He led the Muslim army to several significant victories against the forces of Constantine IV of Byzantium during the Second Arab-Byzantine War. Marwan was succeeded by his son, Abd al-Malik.

historical_references.reference: Marwan II, known as Marwan ibn Muhammad al-Himarī or Marwan the Epic, was the Umayyad Caliph who reigned from 744 to 750 CE. He faced several rebellions, including that of the Berber general, 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi. Marwan was killed during a battle against the rebellion led by Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf in Kufa.
